overview: A single State Department letter concerning postwar civil aviation policy in occupied Japan and southern Korea. Edwin M. Martin asks Arthur C. Bunce whether the Department should prepare a separate policy paper for civil airline operations in southern Korea, noting that Northwest plans to serve Seoul and that the military government has already approved the proposed flights.

subfiles.title: Letter from Martin to Bunce on civil aviation policy for southern Korea
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.to: Arthur C. Bunce, Economic Adviser, Staff of XXIV Corps
subfiles.about: Martin requests Bunce's judgment on whether the State Department should issue a civil aviation policy paper for southern Korea.
subfiles.summary: The State Department is preparing a policy governing the entry and operation of international civil airlines in Japan, where domestic airlines are not expected in the near future. Martin reports that Northwest will also serve Seoul and that the military government has approved flights expected to begin in late spring or early summer. Because occupation conditions in southern Korea differ from those in Japan, he asks Bunce whether a separate Korean civil aviation policy paper would be advisable.

interest: The letter documents the practical formation of American civil aviation policy during the Allied occupations of Japan and southern Korea. It is particularly useful for showing how officials distinguished the two occupation regimes while considering an airline network that crossed between them. Its reference to Northwest's proposed Seoul service and prior military-government approval also supplies evidence about the anticipated timing and administrative preparation of postwar commercial flights.
